text: A pipeline step is idempotent if running it twice with the same input produces the same result as running it once. This matters constantly in real pipelines, because reruns are normal — a scheduled job that failed halfway, or a manual rerun after a bugfix, shouldn't leave the target worse off than before.

Here's the problem in practice. load_append_only uses if_exists equals append. Run it once against orders.csv and the warehouse has eighteen rows. Run it again — because the schedule fired twice, or someone reran it by hand — and now there are thirty-six rows, eighteen of them exact duplicates. Append has no idea the data was already loaded.

The fix is to upsert on order_id instead. The table gets order_id as its PRIMARY KEY, and the insert uses SQLite's INSERT OR REPLACE — if a row with that order_id already exists, it's replaced in place; if it's new, it's inserted. Run this against the same data any number of times and nothing duplicates.

That's the whole mechanism in three steps: key already exists, replace it in place. Key is new, insert it. Run the whole thing again, and the table still ends up with exactly one row per order_id. That's what makes this Load step idempotent.

Because load_upsert is idempotent, recovering from almost any failure is the same story every time: catch the exception, print that it's safe to rerun, then re-raise so the failure is still visible. There's no need to figure out exactly which rows made it in before the crash — rerunning the full batch just re-upserts everything, with no duplicates.

Validation, loading, watermarks, idempotency — every piece from this chapter is sitting in its own function right now. Next lesson wires all of them together into one real, config-driven script you could actually run and schedule.
